lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Tomorrow's Leftovers. Cooking with ingredients that don't exist yet.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: This is Tomorrow's Leftovers. I'm Chef Anselm Brodequin, and I've already eaten.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Tomorrow's Leftovers. Best before: soon.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Tomorrow's Leftovers! Please wash your hands.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: They already have, Pip.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Please wash them again.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Good morning, and welcome to Breakfast Tomorrow. Tomorrow's breakfast, made today, so that tomorrow, you can have a lie-in.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: A word on toast. In this kitchen, we toast the bread before it's sliced, and we slice it before it's baked.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Chef, that's backwards.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: That's breakfast, Pip.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: It's a lot of crumbs, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Today's breakfast forecast. Tomorrow morning, you'll say you want a fry-up. You don't. You want porridge. I've seen it.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Make the porridge. You'll thank me around ten past eight.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Hi! It's Pip Cooks Today, where I cook with things that are actually here!

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Quaint.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Today I'm making a cheese sandwich. Here is the bread. It exists. Here is the cheese. It also exists.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Remarkable. And when will you eat it?

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Now.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Now. Goodness. Just like that. No waiting.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: That's how sandwiches work, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: In your day, perhaps.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Chef's asked me to remind everyone that this is my show, and he's only here to observe.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: I'm not observing, Pip. I'm remembering. I remember this sandwich from Friday. You drop it.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: I'm not going to drop it.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: I dropped it.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: On Friday. You're early.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Good evening. This is The Midnight Larder. Somewhere, very soon, you are going to want a sandwich. We're ready.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: The Midnight Larder is for the night workers. The bakers. The nurses. The person on that relay ship, with a kettle and a long shift ahead of them.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: I've made you a sandwich. It'll be ready at about four. You'll know when.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: A thought for the small hours. Midnight snacking is not a weakness. It is tomorrow's lunch, arriving early, to see if you're in.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: That's beautiful, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: It's cheese, Pip.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Tonight's dish is a Sunday roast. Not this Sunday. The one after, when your aunt visits. Pip, the ingredients.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Yes, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Tonight, a soup that by next week is going to be quite famous. Get in early. Pip?

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Ready, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Today, a fish pie, made with a fish that is, as we speak, still thinking it over. Aprons on.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Chef, what are we cooking today?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Leftovers, Pip. From a dinner party we're throwing on Saturday. We cook the leftovers first. It saves time.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Now, the eggs. These were laid on Thursday. It's currently Monday. The hen is still thinking about it, so we crack them gently, as a courtesy.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: There's nothing in the bowl, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Crack them anyway, Pip. Confidence.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Chop one onion. It hasn't been grown yet, so you'll be crying in advance. Very efficient.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: I cried about this onion on Saturday. Twice.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: I'm not crying.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: You will be. Wednesday. Something about a film.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Season generously, with salt from the sea we'll be visiting in August.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Can I taste it?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: No need. I tasted it last week. A touch more pepper.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: No. Less. There. Perfect.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Into the oven. Now, our oven timer counts up, not down. We don't take a dish out when it's done. We take it out when we remember it.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: And there's the timer, telling us we've remembered. Lovely.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: For the sauce, one cup of the rain forecast for Sunday. Reduce it over a low heat until it's only a slight chance of rain.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: How will I know when it's ready?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: When you'd take a coat, Pip, but you wouldn't take an umbrella.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Stir clockwise, which in this kitchen is towards next week.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Pip. That is the wrong spoon.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Which one's the right spoon?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: The one you'll pick up on Friday. Until then, do your best with that one.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Fold in the butter. Ours has been softened by a compliment you haven't been paid yet. Somebody, soon, is going to tell you that you look well. That's what's in this.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: That's lovely, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: That's chemistry, Pip.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Let it rest. Everything needs a rest. The dough. The meat. You, Pip. I've seen next week, and you're going to want this ten minutes back.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Thank you, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: And there we are. I tasted this on Friday. Magnificent. Pip, try some.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: It isn't cooked yet, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Then you'll have to trust me.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Serve immediately. Or, as I prefer, slightly before.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Whatever's left over, we'll eat tonight, which is how we got the leftovers in the first place. Goodnight.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Chef, how many does it serve?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Four. Five, if your cousin turns up. He will. Make it five.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: People ask me, Chef, how do you taste a dish before it's cooked?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: And I tell them: the same way you miss someone before they've left. You simply know it's coming, and you make room.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Chef, the jar on the top shelf that says Soup, Later. Can I open it?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Not yet, Pip. It's labelled for a reason.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: When's later?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Ask me later.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: A note on allergies. Some of tonight's dishes may contain traces of next week. If you're sensitive to next week, please, take it one day at a time.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: A letter! Dear Chef, I followed your recipe for Wednesday's casserole, and now it's Wednesday, and I'm not hungry. What do I do?

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Freeze it. Thursday will be very grateful. Thursday always is.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Burnt toast is a disappointment. Unless, of course, you saw it coming.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Introducing Brodequin's Pre-Burnt Toast. We've burnt it for you, in advance, so the disappointment is already over, and all that's left is breakfast.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Pre-Burnt Toast may contain toast.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Tonight's programme is brought to you by Grumbel's Ladders.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: Every kitchen has a top shelf. And on every top shelf, there's a jar of the good jam, put there by someone who didn't want you to have it.

lines.speaker: Arnold Grumbel
lines.text: The Grumbel's Pantry Step. Three rungs. Very quiet. Nobody needs to know.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. Jam is a reward.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Tomorrow's Leftovers, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: A Listener, Calling From Next Week
lines.text: Hello, Chef. It's me, from next week. I'm just ringing to say the soup was lovely.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Thank you. I know.

lines.speaker: A Listener, Calling From Next Week
lines.text: I know you know. I just wanted to say it in person. Well, in advance.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Very good of you. Any notes?

lines.speaker: A Listener, Calling From Next Week
lines.text: Only one. Tell Pip about the spoon.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: We've covered the spoon.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: We haven't, really, Chef.

lines.speaker: A Listener, Calling From Next Week
lines.text: You will. Bye now.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: This week we're carving a pumpkin that will be grown in time for next year's Halloween. Pip, the pumpkin.

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: There's no pumpkin, Chef.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Then carve the space where the pumpkin will be. Bigger smile.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: There. Terrifying.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Pumpkin soup, for Halloween night. I've tasted it already. Rich. Warming. A little spooky.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Something in it was looking back at me.

lines.speaker: Chef Anselm Brodequin
lines.text: Pip, did you carve a face in the soup?

lines.speaker: Pip, the Sous-Chef
lines.text: Only a small one, Chef.
